title: A loop is not a permanent knot
hook: Which manipulation removes the drawn crossing?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: A crossing in a two-dimensional drawing is not enough to prove a knot. This open loop can be slid over an accessible end, removing the shown crossing without cutting the cord.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.
objective: A crossing in a two-dimensional drawing is not enough to prove a knot. This open loop can be slid over an accessible end, removing the shown crossing without cutting the cord.

claims.text: A crossing in a two-dimensional drawing is not enough to prove a knot. This open loop can be slid over an accessible end, removing the shown crossing without cutting the cord.
claims.source: W-383 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): retyped from source (Raymer & Smith 2007, which could not be opened from this host) to derivation, as FC LH-1 and FC LH-2 asked. Argument: the drawn curl is a one-crossing diagram of an open arc (a Reidemeister I kink). A one-crossing diagram is never a knot, so the crossing alone does not prove a knot. The cord has a free end, so the loop can be slid along the cord and off that end, which removes the crossing without cutting; on the stage the free end (15 to 35 cm on the slider) always exceeds the 10 cm loop travel (src/lib/lifehacks/home-models.ts evaluateHome, homeCordScene). Earlier history: FC LH-2 held it unverified only because its sole source was unopenable. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read the cord scene in HomeLesson.tsx and homeCordScene first. Derivation: an arc with free ends is unknotted (any tangle in an open string can be undone by moving an end), and the drawn curl is a one-crossing kink (Reidemeister I), so one crossing never proves a knot. Own run of the transpiled home-models.ts: crossings = 1 before and 0 after 'Slide loop off'. The free end minus the start is 3p px for p = 15 to 35 cm, always more than the 10 cm loop travel (30 px). The reveal shows spec.idea, the claim text. No source is relied on.

claims.text: Plain cord; storage only. The drawing gives no electrical safety limit or product-specific bend radius.
claims.source: Scope limits and illustrative assumptions of this card; Depicted crossings=1 or0; available free end=input cm, required loop travel=10cm. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: stage caption reads "Plain cord; storage only" and the reveal limit matches word for word (390x844 screenshots, both states); homeCordScene draws only a path, a grey ellipse, an arrow, dots and a bracket: no plug, device or limit value.

claims.text: Depicted crossings=1 or0; available free end=input cm, required loop travel=10cm.
claims.source: Computed in src/lib/lifehacks/home-models.ts; all dimensions and rates are stated on the stage. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: re-ran evaluateHome and homeCordScene for p=15..35, both states: drawn crossings = value = 1 before, 0 after (0 mismatches); stage readout "Loop travel=10cm · end=Ncm" matches; slider min 15 cm > 10 cm travel, so the slide is always possible on this slider. Minor drawing note: the orange crossing dot is at y=125 but the two segments cross at y=116.7. W-383 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): the crossing dot is now drawn at the true crossing (150, 350/3 ≈ 116.7) instead of (150,125); the count of drawn crossings is unchanged.

claims.text: Which manipulation removes the drawn crossing?
claims.source: Chosen comparison question; the prediction refers to the stated default values and selected methods. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified: the rendered predict and stage question; key = 1 "Slide loop off", which is the manipulation that removes the crossing (threading the end through the loop would add crossings, tying an overhand).

claims.text: A crossing in a drawing does not prove a knot. An open loop can slide off an accessible end, and the crossing disappears without cutting.
claims.source: Recall transfer item for this lesson; scenario values are stipulated in the question. The why applies the lesson's own model and limits (see this lesson's idea, limit and formula claims). Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-2 (2026-10-14, fresh fact-checker instance, W-369): verified by derivation: a one-crossing curl in an open cord is not a knot and slides off an accessible end; keyed option 1 "Not if the loop slides off the free end" matches; both distractors are false.

recall.question: A drawn cord crosses over itself, and the loop's free end is within reach. What does the lesson say about whether this is a knot?
options: Yes: one crossing is enough to prove a knot
Not if the loop slides off the free end
Yes: only cutting can remove the crossing
recall.why: A crossing in a drawing does not prove a knot. An open loop can slide off an accessible end, and the crossing disappears without cutting.
